searchText: Thanks for the info! If I understand correctly then from an application perspective it does still make sense to count confirmations (as it was usually done with PoW) as a less secure but faster algorithm to establish "finality", right? Circle still seems to do it https://developers.circle.com/developer/docs/confirmations If you refer to > Ethereum (USDC, EUROC, ETH) 12 ~3 minutes it definitely looks like stale docs. With no missed slots 12 slots = 2.4min, where 12 pre-merge block times are indeed 12min. In PoW the economic security guarantee of a block increases somewhat linearly with each new block. In Ethereum PoS it's more complicated, with more instances of very non-linear behavior. For example this post explains a patched issue of the fork-choice that allowed 10 slot deep re-orgs at low cost https://blog.ethereum.org/2023/05/03/secured-5-disclosures-update Thank you. What I'm trying to find out is if it makes sense for any application then to do the PoW-style probabilistic block confirmation waiting game. (Sounds like it doesn't?) In general it doesn’t, but in the happy case it kinda of does. (You definitely shouldn’t rely on this though.) As <@602753420033785856> mentioned there has been a bunch of work that has gone into these more advanced algorithms, but they are not deployed yet. Thanks for the clarification! Always better to make use of the finality gadget to be on the safe side then I guess.

excerpts.author: dapplion
excerpts.content:
If you refer to

> Ethereum (USDC, EUROC, ETH)    12    ~3 minutes

it definitely looks like stale docs. With no missed slots 12 slots = 2.4min, where 12 pre-merge block times are indeed 12min.

In PoW the economic security guarantee of a block increases somewhat linearly with each new block. In Ethereum PoS it's more complicated, with more instances of very non-linear behavior. For example this post explains a patched issue of the fork-choice that allowed 10 slot deep re-orgs at low cost https://blog.ethereum.org/2023/05/03/secured-5-disclosures-update

excerpts.content: In general it doesn’t, but in the happy case it kinda of does. (You definitely shouldn’t rely on this though.) As <@602753420033785856> mentioned there has been a bunch of work that has gone into these more advanced algorithms, but they are not deployed yet.
